patch.value: Add fail-closed docstring, duplication, lint, and authored-TypeScript gates

The package has exact fail-closed runtime coverage, but its release gate does not yet mechanically enforce repo-wide docstring coverage, authored-source TypeScript-only policy, duplication thresholds, or a strict lint rule set. The tracked dist/index.js is generated and required for git-URL consumers; the authored prepare hook is migrated to TypeScript in pm-ts-starter-sirq. Add gates that distinguish required generated output from authored source and cannot be bypassed by narrowing file lists.

A directory-discovered fail-closed gate proves 100% high-quality docstring coverage for all authored source declarations; authored JS/MJS/CJS/HTML files fail while required generated dist output is reproducibly build-verified; strict TypeScript/ESLint and duplication gates cover all authored source and tests without frozen allowlists; package and CI release checks run the gates on Node 22 and 26; real tests remain exact 100/100/100 with zero skips
Select maintained TypeScript-compatible lint, docstring, and duplication tooling after inspecting their real installed types/configuration; define generated-output exception narrowly for dist
Local release:check and GitHub Actions Node 22/26
Inspect package scripts and CI: exact coverage is enforced, but no docstring, lint, duplication, or authored-language gate is invoked
Every mandatory source-quality policy fails closed in local and CI release gates
Exact source coverage passes, and the authored lifecycle hook is TypeScript, but the remaining source-quality policies are review conventions rather than executable gates
Undocumented, duplicated, or policy-incompatible authored code can regress without failing release checks
